summary: Retrom is a self-hosted server and frontend designed for distributing and launching private game libraries. It functions as a centralised hub to manage and stream your game collection across devices from your own infrastructure. Built with Rust and distributed as a container, it handles the backend organisation and client-side access for self-hosters.
goodFor: Self-hosters who want a dedicated, private alternative to commercial platforms for organising and streaming their personal digital game archives.
watchOut: The project has a moderate maintenance tempo and occupies a crowded niche, meaning you may encounter rough edges or less community documentation compared to mature alternatives.
deployNotes: As a Docker-based application, you will need to configure persistent volumes for your game library data and metadata storage. You should also place the container behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination for secure remote access.
